stage_b_reviewed_content.statement:
Let $(A, \text{d})$ be a differential graded algebra. Let $E$ be a compact
object of $D(A, \text{d})$. Let $P$ be a differential graded $A$-module
which has a finite filtration
$$
0 = F_{-1}P \subset F_0P \subset F_1P \subset \ldots \subset F_nP = P
$$
by differential graded submodules such that
$$
F_{i + 1}P/F_iP \cong \bigoplus\nolimits_{j \in J_i} A[k_{i, j}]
$$
as differential graded $A$-modules for some sets $J_i$ and integers $k_{i, j}$.
Let $E \to P$ be a morphism of $D(A, \text{d})$.
Then there exists a differential graded submodule $P' \subset P$ such that
$F_{i + 1}P \cap P'/(F_iP \cap P')$ is equal to
$\bigoplus_{j \in J'_i} A[k_{i, j}]$ for some finite subsets
$J'_i \subset J_i$ and such that $E \to P$ factors through $P'$.

Let $E \to P$ be a morphism of $D(A, \text{d})$.

reason: Inductively shrinks an n-step cellular dg module by selecting finitely many generators at each filtration level whose differentials land in previously selected lower cells. Compactness makes the given E→P factor through the finitely selected quotient at each step, yielding a genuine dg submodule with finite cells.

stage_b_reviewed_content.statement:
Let $(A, \text{d})$ be a differential graded algebra. Let $E$ be an
object of $D(A, \text{d})$. Then the following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item $E$ is a compact object,
\item $E$ is a direct summand of an object of $D(A, \text{d})$
which is represented by a differential graded module $P$ which
has a finite filtration $F_\bullet$ by differential graded submodules
such that $F_iP/F_{i - 1}P$ are finite direct sums of shifts of $A$.
\end{enumerate}
hypotheses:
Let $(A, \text{d})$ be a differential graded algebra. Let $E$ be an
object of $D(A, \text{d})$.
conclusions:
The following conditions are equivalent: \begin{enumerate}
\item $E$ is a compact object,
\item $E$ is a direct summand of an object of $D(A, \text{d})$
which is represented by a differential graded module $P$ which
has a finite filtration $F_\bullet$ by differential graded submodules
such that $F_iP/F_{i - 1}P$ are finite direct sums of shifts of $A$.
\end{enumerate}

reason: A compact E with property-(P) representative P has identity factoring through a finite sum of cellular filtration stages via the telescope triangle and compactness. The preceding finite-subcell factorization gives a retract of a finite-cell dg module. Conversely finite sums of shifts A[k] are compact, and finite extensions and retracts preserve compactness.

stage_b_reviewed_content.statement:
Let $(A, \text{d})$ be a differential graded algebra.
For every compact object $E$ of $D(A, \text{d})$ there
exist integers $a \leq b$ such that $\Hom_{D(A, \text{d})}(E, M) = 0$
if $H^i(M) = 0$ for $i \in [a, b]$.
hypotheses: Let $(A, \text{d})$ be a differential graded algebra.
conclusions:
For every compact object $E$ of $D(A, \text{d})$ there
exist integers $a \leq b$ such that $\Hom_{D(A, \text{d})}(E, M) = 0$
if $H^i(M) = 0$ for $i \in [a, b]$.

reason: The class of source objects whose derived Hom vanishes when target cohomology vanishes in a finite interval is thick and triangulated; the compact-object finite-cell characterization reduces to the shift of free rank-one A, for which Hom_D(A,M)=H^0(M), establishing the finite-window statement.

stage_b_reviewed_content.statement:
Let $(A, \text{d})$ be a differential graded algebra. Assume that $A^n = 0$
for $|n| \gg 0$. Let $E$ be an object of $D(A, \text{d})$.
The following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item $E$ is a compact object, and
\item $E$ can be represented by a differential graded $A$-module $P$
which is finite projective as a graded $A$-module and satisfies
$\Hom_{K(A, \text{d})}(P, M) = \Hom_{D(A, \text{d})}(P, M)$
for every differential graded $A$-module $M$.
\end{enumerate}
hypotheses:
Let $(A, \text{d})$ be a differential graded algebra. Assume that $A^n = 0$
for $|n| \gg 0$. Let $E$ be an object of $D(A, \text{d})$.
conclusions:
The following conditions are equivalent: \begin{enumerate}
\item $E$ is a compact object, and
\item $E$ can be represented by a differential graded $A$-module $P$
which is finite projective as a graded $A$-module and satisfies
$\Hom_{K(A, \text{d})}(P, M) = \Hom_{D(A, \text{d})}(P, M)$
for every differential graded $A$-module $M$.
\end{enumerate}

reason: The proof uses a finite-cell retract and an iterative cone construction to represent E⊕E[n] by a finite graded free dg module, then cuts away distant degrees by graded-projective splitting. However pinned source line 6455 claims b−n+2c≥a−2c, whereas its earlier choice n>b+4c−a gives the strict reverse inequality. Since this inequality drives surjectivity of P1⊕P2→P, the source needs correction before a clean proof-screen verdict.
